## data import and cleaning

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(zoo)

# Step 1: Load data and add league + season info
champ24 <- read_csv("Data/Champ23-24.csv") |>
  mutate(League = "Championship", Season = "23-24")

prem24 <- read_csv("Data/prem 2023-2024.csv") |>
  mutate(League = "Premier League", Season = "23-24")

league_one24 <- read_csv("Data/League one 23-24.csv") |>
  mutate(League = "League one", Season = "23-24")


prem25 <- read_csv("Data/prem 2024-2025.csv") |>
  mutate(League = "Premier League", Season = "24-25")

champ25 <- read_csv("Data/Champ24-25.csv") |>
  mutate(League = "Championship", Season = "24-25")

league_one25 <- read_csv("Data/League one 24-25.csv") |>
  mutate(League = "League one", Season = "24-25")

# Combine all seasons
season_all <- bind_rows(champ24, prem25, champ25)

season_all_2 <- bind_rows(league_one24, league_one25, champ24, champ25, prem24, prem25)

# Step 2: Create goal columns for home and away teams and opponent goals
season_all <- season_all |>
  mutate(
    HomeTeam_Goals = FTHG,
    AwayTeam_Goals = FTAG,
    HomeTeam_OpponentGoals = FTAG,  # Goals conceded by home team
    AwayTeam_OpponentGoals = FTHG   # Goals conceded by away team
  )

# Step 3: Pivot to long format
matches_long <- season_all |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(HomeTeam_Goals, AwayTeam_Goals),
    names_to = "TeamType",
    values_to = "Goals"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Team = if_else(TeamType == "HomeTeam_Goals", HomeTeam, AwayTeam),
    Opponent = if_else(TeamType == "HomeTeam_Goals", AwayTeam, HomeTeam),
    Home = if_else(TeamType == "HomeTeam_Goals", 1, 0),
    Opponent_Goals = if_else(TeamType == "HomeTeam_Goals", 
                             HomeTeam_OpponentGoals, 
                             AwayTeam_OpponentGoals)
  )

# Step 4: Convert factors explicitly and set levels (important for predict later)
matches_long <- matches_long |>
  mutate(
    League = factor(League),
    Season = factor(Season),
    Team = factor(Team),
    Opponent = factor(Opponent)
  )

# Step 5: Calculate points per match (3 win, 1 draw, 0 loss)
matches_long <- matches_long |>
  mutate(
    Points = case_when(
      Goals > Opponent_Goals ~ 3,
      Goals == Opponent_Goals ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

# Step 6: Calculate rolling form **within each Season and Team**

matches_long <- matches_long |>
  arrange(Season, Team, Date) |>
  group_by(Season, Team) |>
  mutate(
    form_pts_last5 = lag(rollapply(Points, width = 5, FUN = sum, fill = NA, align = "right"))
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Step 7: Calculate rolling form for Opponents (also within Season)
matches_long <- matches_long |>
  arrange(Season, Opponent, Date) |>
  group_by(Season, Opponent) |>
  mutate(
    opp_form_pts_last5 = lag(rollapply(Points, width = 5, FUN = sum, fill = NA, align = "right"))
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Step 8: Filter rows with no missing form data
model_data <- matches_long |>
  filter(!is.na(form_pts_last5), !is.na(opp_form_pts_last5))

# Make sure factors keep the same levels as in the original data to avoid errors in predict
model_data <- model_data |>
  mutate(
    Team = factor(Team, levels = levels(matches_long$Team)),
    Opponent = factor(Opponent, levels = levels(matches_long$Opponent)),
    League = factor(League, levels = levels(matches_long$League)),
    Season = factor(Season, levels = levels(matches_long$Season))
  )

```

## Poisson models

```{r}

glm_model <- glm(  Goals ~ League * Team + League * Opponent + Home + Season * Team,
  data = matches_long,
  family = poisson(link = "log")
)

summary(glm_model)
```

```{r}
glm_model_2 <- glm(
  Goals ~ League * Team + League * Opponent + Home + Season * Team + 
    form_pts_last5 + opp_form_pts_last5,
  data = model_data,
  family = poisson(link = "log")
)

summary(glm_model_2)
```

```{r}
glm_model_2_all <- glm(
  Goals ~ League * Team + League * Opponent + Home + Season * Team + 
    form_pts_last5 + opp_form_pts_last5,
  data = model_data_2,
  family = poisson(link = "log")
)

summary(glm_model_2_all)
```

## Goal prediction

```{r}
# Step 5: Predict expected goals for an upcoming match

# Prepare new match data for prediction
# Example: Ipswich (home) vs Bristol City (away)
new_match_home <- tibble(
  Home = 1,
  League = factor("Championship", levels = levels(matches_long$League)),
  Season = factor("24-25", levels = levels(matches_long$Season)),
  Team = factor("Bromley", levels = levels(matches_long$Team)),
  Opponent = factor("Ipswich", levels = levels(matches_long$Opponent)),
  form_pts_last5 = 0,      # example form points Bristol City last 5 matches
  opp_form_pts_last5 = 0 )

new_match_away <- tibble(
  Home = 0,
  League = factor("Championship", levels = levels(matches_long$League)),
  Season = factor("24-25", levels = levels(matches_long$Season)),
  Team = factor("Ipswich", levels = levels(matches_long$Team)),
  Opponent = factor("Bromley", levels = levels(matches_long$Opponent)),
    form_pts_last5 = 0,      # example form points Bristol City last 5 matches
  opp_form_pts_last5 = 0   # example form points Ipswich last 5 matches
)

expected_goals_home <- predict(glm_model_2, newdata = new_match_home, type = "response") #change glm_model_2 if form isnt a better predictor
expected_goals_away <- predict(glm_model_2, newdata = new_match_away, type = "response")

print(paste("Expected goals for wat (home):", round(expected_goals_home, 2)))
print(paste("Expected goals for sot (away):", round(expected_goals_away, 2)))
```

## Train-test Split

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# 1. Split data
train_data <- model_data_2 |> filter(Season == "23-24")
test_data <- model_data_2 |> filter(Season == "24-25")

# 2. Ensure relevant columns are factors in training
train_data$Team <- factor(train_data$Team)
train_data$Opponent <- factor(train_data$Opponent)
train_data$League <- factor(train_data$League)

# 3. Match factor levels in test set
test_data$Team <- factor(test_data$Team, levels = levels(train_data$Team))
test_data$Opponent <- factor(test_data$Opponent, levels = levels(train_data$Opponent))
test_data$League <- factor(test_data$League, levels = levels(train_data$League))

# 4. Remove problematic teams from test_data
problem_teams <- c("Derby", "Oxford", "Portsmouth")
test_data <- test_data |> 
  filter(!(Team %in% problem_teams | Opponent %in% problem_teams))

# 5. Train model
train_model <- glm(
  Goals ~ League * Team + League * Opponent + Home + form_pts_last5 + opp_form_pts_last5,
  data = train_data,
  family = poisson(link = "log")
)

# 6. Prepare test_data for prediction:
# Assuming test_data already has HomeTeam and AwayTeam columns matching Team/Opponent
# If not, create them here (uncomment if needed)
# test_data <- test_data %>%
#   rename(HomeTeam = Team, AwayTeam = Opponent)

# 7. Filter test_data for known teams only (safety)
known_teams <- levels(train_data$Team)
test_data_filtered <- test_data %>%
  filter(HomeTeam %in% known_teams, AwayTeam %in% known_teams)

# 8. Create prediction datasets
home_pred_data <- test_data_filtered %>%
  transmute(
    Date, Season, League,
    Team = HomeTeam,
    Opponent = AwayTeam,
    Home = 1,
    form_pts_last5,
    opp_form_pts_last5
  )

away_pred_data <- test_data_filtered %>%
  transmute(
    Date, Season, League,
    Team = AwayTeam,
    Opponent = HomeTeam,
    Home = 0,
    form_pts_last5,
    opp_form_pts_last5
  )

# 9. Align factor levels
home_pred_data$Team <- factor(home_pred_data$Team, levels = levels(train_data$Team))
home_pred_data$Opponent <- factor(home_pred_data$Opponent, levels = levels(train_data$Opponent))
home_pred_data$League <- factor(home_pred_data$League, levels = levels(train_data$League))

away_pred_data$Team <- factor(away_pred_data$Team, levels = levels(train_data$Team))
away_pred_data$Opponent <- factor(away_pred_data$Opponent, levels = levels(train_data$Opponent))
away_pred_data$League <- factor(away_pred_data$League, levels = levels(train_data$League))

# 10. Predict goals
home_pred_data$pred_goals <- predict(train_model, newdata = home_pred_data, type = "response")
away_pred_data$pred_goals <- predict(train_model, newdata = away_pred_data, type = "response")

# 11. Combine predictions with actuals
predictions <- test_data_filtered %>%
  select(Date, Season, League, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG) %>%
  mutate(
    pred_FTHG = home_pred_data$pred_goals,
    pred_FTAG = away_pred_data$pred_goals,
    pred_FTHG_round = round(pred_FTHG),
    pred_FTAG_round = round(pred_FTAG)
  )

# 12. Helper function to determine match result
get_result <- function(home_goals, away_goals) {
  if (is.na(home_goals) | is.na(away_goals)) return(NA)
  if (home_goals > away_goals) "home_win"
  else if (home_goals == away_goals) "draw"
  else "away_win"
}

# 13. Calculate actual and predicted results and correctness
predictions <- predictions %>%
  mutate(
    actual_result = mapply(get_result, FTHG, FTAG),
    predicted_result = mapply(get_result, pred_FTHG_round, pred_FTAG_round),
    exact_score_correct = (pred_FTHG_round == FTHG) & (pred_FTAG_round == FTAG),
    outcome_correct = (predicted_result == actual_result)
  )

# 14. Filter predictions for Norwich and Ipswich matches only
norwich_ipswich_preds <- predictions %>%
  filter(HomeTeam %in% c("Norwich", "Ipswich") | AwayTeam %in% c("Norwich", "Ipswich"))

# 15. Assign points: 3 for exact score, 1 for correct outcome
norwich_ipswich_preds <- norwich_ipswich_preds %>%
  mutate(
    points = case_when(
      exact_score_correct ~ 3,
      outcome_correct ~ 1,
      TRUE ~ 0
    )
  )

# 16. Summarize results
total_points <- sum(norwich_ipswich_preds$points, na.rm = TRUE)
exact_correct <- sum(norwich_ipswich_preds$exact_score_correct, na.rm = TRUE)
outcome_correct <- sum(norwich_ipswich_preds$outcome_correct, na.rm = TRUE)
total_matches <- nrow(norwich_ipswich_preds)

cat("Norwich & Ipswich matches evaluated:", total_matches, "\n")
cat("Exact score predictions correct:", exact_correct, "\n")
cat("Correct outcome predictions:", outcome_correct, "\n")
cat("Total points scored:", total_points, "\n")

# 17. Optional: View the detailed table
print(norwich_ipswich_preds %>%
  select(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, FTHG, FTAG, pred_FTHG_round, pred_FTAG_round, exact_score_correct, outcome_correct, points))

```

```{r}
sum(is.na(predictions$FTHG))     # Check actual home goals NA count
sum(is.na(predictions$FTAG))     # Check actual away goals NA count
sum(is.na(predictions$pred_FTHG_round))  # Check predicted home goals NA count
sum(is.na(predictions$pred_FTAG_round))
```

```{r}
  Team = factor("Hull", levels = levels(matches_long$Team)),
  Opponent = factor("Millwall", levels = levels(matches_long$Opponent)),

  opp_form_pts_last5 = 0 )

train_match_away <- tibble(
  Home = 0,
  League = factor("Championship", levels = levels(matches_long$League)),
  Season = factor("24-25", levels = levels(matches_long$Season)),
  Team = factor("Millwall", levels = levels(matches_long$Team)),
  Opponent = factor("Hull", levels = levels(matches_long$Opponent)),
    form_pts_last5 = 0,      # example form points Bristol City last 5 matches
  opp_form_pts_last5 =  2  # example form points Ipswich last 5 matches
)

train_expected_goals_home <- predict(train_model, newdata = train_match_home, type = "response") #change glm_model_2 if form isnt a better predictor

print(paste("Expected goals for Hull (home):", round(train_expected_goals_home, 2)))
print(paste("Expected goals for Millwall (away):", round(train_expected_goals_away, 2)))
```
